result.topic_en: A brief note on finding the maximum of a function f(a,b,c) subject to the constraint a^2+b^2+c^2 = const, giving the resulting condition on the partial derivatives.
result.transcription:
$f(a,b,c)$ = Max[?] $a^2+b^2+c^2 = \text{const}$
$\frac{1}{a}\frac{\partial f}{\partial a} = \frac{1}{b}\frac{\partial f}{\partial b} = [-\ldots-] \frac{1}{c}\frac{\partial f}{\partial c}$

methods.what: Condition for a constrained extremum of f(a,b,c) on the sphere a^2+b^2+c^2 = const (Lagrange multiplier condition: gradient of f parallel to (a,b,c))
methods.quote: $\frac{1}{a}\frac{\partial f}{\partial a} = \frac{1}{b}\frac{\partial f}{\partial b} = [-\ldots-] \frac{1}{c}\frac{\partial f}{\partial c}$

items.english: f(a,b,c) = maximum, subject to a^2+b^2+c^2 = const.
